clue.text: Set out to accept concessions brought back from management

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the jumbled outer word swallows the other piece
brought back means carried the other way, so the word for concessions is read from right to left

parts.note: set down, as a table is set or laid

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed from its place, so the word meaning set gets jumbled

parts.note: sops are small concessions offered to placate someone

explanation.surface: A labour negotiation where the bosses are made to hand back the concessions they had won.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram works on a synonym rather than the printed word: LAID rearranged makes DIAL, which then holds SPOS to give DISPOSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something at your disposal means having control of it, so the word can mean arrangement or control of affairs.

clue.text: Poins is quick to respond to unionist's extempore speech

parts.note: the setter Poins speaking of himself: I am, shortened to I'm
prompt means acting without delay
U is the standard abbreviation for Unionist

explanation.surface: A boast that the setter can match a Unionist politician's speech with a fast retort.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym; here Poins is converted to I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is something spoken or performed without preparation, exactly what an extempore talk is.

clue.text: Each god receives enthusiastic praise

indicators.note: a receiver takes something inside, so the god's name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
ea is the usual abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Every deity is treated to a round of eager adulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean was originally a hymn of thanks to Apollo and now means any song or speech of glowing tribute.

clue.text: His Excellency held captive by crazy purser on old hulk for instance

indicators.note: a captive is held inside, so the title abbreviation sits within the jumbled letters
crazy means wild and disordered, so the purser's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, a ship's officer in charge of accounts
HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, the style of an ambassador or governor
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A diplomat is held prisoner by a deranged ship's officer aboard a rotting old vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hulk' looks like a ship to go with purser, but it is the Incredible Hulk, the Marvel character; the old hulk of the surface is a decaying vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incredible Hulk is one example of a comic-book hero with extraordinary powers, hence 'for instance'.

clue.text: Weapon having greater than average range seen on front of ship

parts.note: long means extending further than usual
the bow is the forward end of a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship's forward gun is described as reaching further than most.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests naval artillery, but the weapon is the archer's English bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The longbow was a tall bow drawn by hand, famously used by English archers at Agincourt.

clue.text: Act nervously when Jack Bishop leaves full of anger

indicators.note: when one person leaves another arrives, so one letter departs and a new one takes its place

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
B is the chess notation for bishop
bitter means resentful and angry

explanation.surface: A card player behaves anxiously once the bishop storms off in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: J replaces B at the start of BITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To jitter is to behave in a jumpy, fidgety way, the physical show of anxiety.

clue.text: Stuff mostly found on a container of varnish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for stuff is dropped

parts.note: to stuff is to cram or jam
a pan is a cooking container

explanation.surface: Most of the material discovered on a tin of wood finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above, so the shortened word sits on top of the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a hard black lacquer, named after the country whose lacquerware it imitated, and as a verb means to coat with it.

clue.text: Incredible to authorise an unreasonably difficult assignment

parts.note: a tall story is one hard to believe
to order is to command or sanction

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at being asked to sign off on an impossible task.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is excessive or very hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Behave theatrically becoming faint right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so the abbreviation for right is taken out

parts.note: a faint chance is a remote chance
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An actor overacts the moment they feel like swooning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately', but it splits into R and the instruction to remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion in an exaggerated, stagey way, as a hammy actor does.

clue.text: Board standing by increase in maintenance costs

parts.note: to up something is to raise it
board and keep both mean the cost of food and lodging

explanation.surface: A company board backs a rise in what it spends on upkeep of its premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee, but it means food and lodging, as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the expense of keeping something in good repair, or the act of maintaining it.

clue.text: Game plan surprisingly holding over time

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the abbreviation
something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
O stands for over in cricket scoring
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A strategy for a match unexpectedly running on into extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPL holds O, then EON follows: NAPOLEON. The surface's game is a sports fixture; the answer is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon, often shortened to nap, is a trick-taking card game similar to whist.

clue.text: Letter signed by many on all sides seen by 4's partner

parts.note: round means surrounding on every side
the answer to 4 is a superhero; Batman's sidekick is the Boy Wonder

explanation.surface: A petition is passed round and spotted by a famous crime-fighter's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 4 down: a superhero's partner is Robin, sidekick of Batman.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a petition with signatures arranged in a circle, so no single signer appears to head the list.

clue.text: Begin with Frank

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a name, Frank seems to be a person; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for starting proceedings and as an adjective for someone candid and unconcealing.

clue.text: Boxes with fasteners essentially in short supply

parts.note: spars is a verb form: a boxer spars in practice

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter of the word is used

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters is its centre

explanation.surface: Crates that come with clips are scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' reads as containers but is a verb for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, which matches a quantity that is scarce.

clue.text: A poem by me about parting to move ahead is a good example to imitate

indicators.note: parting means splitting apart, so the verb is divided to let the other letters in

parts.note: to roll on is to move forward

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the pronoun is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poet invites readers to follow the example of their verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' acts on the pronoun alone, and 'parting' means the verb is split open with the other letters placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others look up to and copy.

clue.text: Renovation of old newel is carried out successfully

indicators.note: a renovation rebuilds and rearranges, so the following letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written; a newel is the post at the foot of a staircase

explanation.surface: Restoring an antique staircase post has been a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Well done describes a task performed skilfully, and is also said as praise for a job accomplished.

clue.text: What Romeo and Juliet made of the vocal Mercutio's initial rollicking

indicators.note: rollicking means boisterous and tumbling about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter, so only the start of the name is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: The star-crossed lovers' response to their loud friend Mercutio's boisterous banter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercutio is Romeo's quick-tongued friend in Shakespeare's play, so the whole surface stays in Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet married purely for passion, the textbook case of a union for romance rather than advantage.

clue.text: Infamous denial by Conservative largely over promises to pay

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: no is a refusal or denial
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's denial sits on top of a pile of unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means placed above, so the IOUs come last.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means widely known for something bad, which is what infamous means.

clue.text: Opening of match factory at last after self-contradictory statement from head of finance

parts.note: an Irish bull is a statement containing a ludicrous contradiction

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the end letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

indicators.note: the head is the top or start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A match factory's launch follows a muddled announcement by the finance chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The match of the surface is a matchstick; the definition's match is a hockey game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully-off is the old method of starting a field hockey match, with two players clashing sticks over the ball.

clue.text: Rex overwhelmed by dad becomes more distant

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so the king's letter is swallowed up

parts.note: a father is a dad
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A boy named Rex is smothered by his father and grows aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex reads as a name but is the king, R, as on royal monograms.
explanation.definitionFit: Farther is the comparative of far, meaning at a greater distance.

clue.text: Extremely gripping — it's a fact

indicators.note: gripping means holding tight, so the word for extremely clasps the following pronoun

parts.note: very means to an extreme degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: An emphatic insistence that something enthralling is the plain truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A verity is a true statement or principle, something established as fact.

clue.text: The same as marks primarily found on fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of marks is used

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Identical spots appear on a fish's scales.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after, so the letter follows the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in references to avoid repeating an author or work.

clue.text: Play God ultimately obliterating half of a Palestinian city

indicators.note: obliterating means wiping out, and here it wipes out half the letters of the city
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of God is used

parts.note: the final letter
Ramallah is a city in the West Bank

explanation.surface: A call for divine destruction of part of a West Bank city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of RAMALLAH is kept and the second half is wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, radio or screen.

clue.text: Guardiola hedging about debut of Moroccan right-winger in final

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so the coach's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is a famous football manager
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of the country is taken

parts.note: the opening letter
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A football manager equivocates over giving a Moroccan winger his first game in a cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's winger and final are football; the right-winger is a political Tory, and final is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A peremptory order or decision is one that admits no appeal or refusal, so it is conclusive and settled.

clue.text: No show flat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without showiness or ornament
second meaning: a level expanse of land

explanation.walkthrough: 'No show' suggests someone failing to turn up and 'flat' an apartment; both are red herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something simple and unadorned, and as a noun names a broad stretch of level country.

clue.text: Turned around drab Australian city

indicators.note: turned around means facing back the other way, so the word for drab is written backwards

parts.note: drab and slut are both old words for a slovenly woman
A is a standard abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A dull antipodean city gets a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian city' seems one phrase, but the city is in Oklahoma and Australian only gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in the US state of Oklahoma, on the Arkansas River.

clue.text: Coin collection's original solid silvery-grey boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the outer words wrap around the letter

parts.note: hard means firm and solid

indicators.note: the original comes first, so only the opening letter of collection is used

parts.note: the first letter
ash is a pale silvery grey colour

explanation.surface: A numismatist's first prize piece is a solid silver-grey boxed set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin collection' looks like one phrase, but Coin alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash is money in coins and notes rather than cheques or credit, and coin as a mass noun means metal money.

clue.text: Legendary hero working in shop

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss archer of legend
on means operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A figure of legend has taken a job behind a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a noun, but it is the slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police, which is what telling on them means.

clue.text: Name attached to oddly ignored offer to bury everyone killed in battle

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so the kept letters surround the next word
ignoring the odd positions leaves only the even-placed letters

parts.note: second and fourth letters
all means everyone
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A grim proposal to inter all the war dead under a named memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: N is attached at the end of F(ALL)E.
explanation.definitionFit: The fallen is the customary term for soldiers who died fighting, as on war memorials.

clue.text: Try to stop soldiers seconds before earl gets run through

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the word for try is wedged in the middle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a judge tries or hears a case
s is the abbreviation for seconds
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An earl is skewered moments after attempting to halt advancing troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' reads as stabbed with a sword, which fits the battle surface, but it means practise; 'Try' is the legal sense of hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance by going over it, which is what running through it means.
